In a single-RSU architecture, sensing observations are dominated by monostatic, radial-velocity components — a geometry that limits motion observability and degrades beam prediction under high mobility and complex road shapes. This work studies predictive beamforming in a distributed multi-RSU ISAC system that jointly exploits monostatic and bistatic sensing, reusing standard OFDM waveforms without dedicated sensing waveforms or extra signaling overhead, and proposes MR-CLNet, a spatio-temporal learning framework that maps multi-RSU observations directly to future beam directions. In simulation it outperforms single-RSU and representative learning-based baselines in angle prediction accuracy and average achievable rate, with the most pronounced gains under high mobility and on curved roads.
